title: Skywork AI Drops Open-Source World Builder, like Google’s Genie 3 but free for devs to create interactive virtual environments from scratch. Huge win for indie creators & open innovation in gaming + simulation.
author: Minimum_Minimum4577

comments.author: name_was_taken
comments.body: It *might* be amazing, but that video isn't proving it.  I can't imagine anyone being impressed with that video with no explanation of what's supposed to be amazing about it.

replies.body: yes , true , lot of them also have an upscaling step to make it look crisp

comments.author: Katwazere
comments.body: It's useless if it can't even remember what each part of the map is and such. It's literally worse in every way than procedural map generation from 15 years ago

replies.author: Samsterdam
replies.body: I wouldn't say that it's useless. Don't forget none of that is generated by an artist. It's all generated per frame and then displayed. Every system that you're talking about that involves procedural generation involves some sort of assets that an artist has created. This method doesn't and that's what is so revolutionary about it. I fully believe that in the next 10 to 15 years we are going to see a reduction in game file sizes while simultaneously seeing an increase in their visual, Fidelity and detail.

comments.body: Ive seen a bunch of this demoes , even with gogle genie , But i dong get how this can be integrated into real game dev , the assets generation is unpredictable , i mean how to do u build the game logic for this ?

replies.author: monsterfurby
replies.body: Yeah, my thoughts exactly. Trying to be everything at once is the same as being a one-trick pony. The benefit of GenAI for gamedev is in building better, smarter tools, not in replacing the toolbox with a one-size-fits-all ready-made project.

replies.author: ninjasaid13
replies.body: yep, unless you have an AI that can create meshes and animation and the environment and the code for the game from just looking at how the generated video behaves, I don't think this is any use for games.

replies.author: superkickstart
replies.body: Ai could be used to generate the underlying "white box" version of the world, but at that point it's probably more practical to use traditional procedural generation methods with ai just assisting. Ai generation is way too finicky to control precicely and it quickly turns into a giant whacamole situation.

replies.author: Tulired
replies.body:
One use for this tech that came to mind with the memory capacity Genie-3 has with updates on memory in intervals from new images is some kind of Enhanced Google Street view especially if you keep it in check where you can go or do. Add people and cars walking around etc. To yhe scenes and you can only deviate a little bit (visible part in the images) from the "path". I feel it would be much more smooth/immersive than the normal street view especially if you have legs etc.

Ofc some kind alternative earth would be fun too
